one-flew-over-the-cuckoo-s-nest-1975.gazette: Production moved into Oregon State Hospital in Salem, where real patients and staff appeared on camera and the institution's own superintendent took a role. The crew worked inside a functioning ward rather than a set dressed to resemble one. What the film calls a ward was, for the duration of the shoot, still a ward.

the-lost-honour-of-katharina-blum-1975.gazette: West Germany in 1975 was in the thick of its RAF years: emergency policing, wiretaps, and a mass-circulation tabloid press led by Bild-Zeitung. Heinrich Böll had already been on the receiving end of that press, denounced in print after questioning how the manhunt was being covered. The novel he wrote in response named the machinery, and the film keeps the names.

the-story-of-adele-h-1975.gazette: Adèle Hugo kept her journals in a private cipher, and they were not fully decoded until more than a century after she wrote them. Those pages track her pursuit of Lieutenant Pinson from Halifax to Barbados, an itinerary the film follows rather than invents. The documents came first; the screenplay works downstream of them.
the-story-of-adele-h-1975.prism: Decoding a private cipher is an act done to someone, not with them. The film's fidelity to the diaries is also the completion of an exposure she spent her life encrypting against.

jeanne-dielman-23-quai-du-commerce-1976.gazette: Akerman gave housework its actual duration — potatoes peeled in full, dishes washed end to end, a bed remade without a cut. Nothing is compressed to signal that time has passed. The runtime is the argument.

kings-of-the-road-1976.gazette: Wenders shot along the West German side of the inner-German border in black and white, working through provincial towns whose cinemas were closing as the crew arrived. The projection booths, the equipment, the empty houses were found rather than built. By the end of the decade many of those screens were dark for good.

harlan-county-usa-1977.gazette: Barbara Kopple's crew stayed in Harlan County, Kentucky through the Brookside strike that began in 1973, filming picket lines, company gun thugs, and union meetings as they happened. The miners and their wives on screen are the strikers themselves, and the UMWA's internal turmoil of those years runs alongside the dispute. A striker was shot dead before the contract was signed.
harlan-county-usa-1977.prism: The camera was not neutral equipment on that road — being filmed changed what men with guns were willing to do in daylight. Documentation and protection turned out to be the same job.

suspiria-1977.gazette: Argento had the film printed by three-strip Technicolor dye transfer, among the last productions to use the process before the labs shut it down. The exteriors were shot at real Freiburg facades, the interiors built and lit in Rome. The color on screen is a chemistry that no longer exists in commercial form.

the-chess-players-1977.gazette: In 1856 the East India Company annexed Awadh and deposed Wajid Ali Shah, its last nawab, on grounds of misgovernment. Ray's film sets the Company's paperwork against two noblemen at a chessboard in Lucknow, both drawn from the historical record of the court. The annexation stands one year before the rebellion of 1857.

watership-down-1978.gazette: Richard Adams set the story on ground he knew — Watership Down is an actual chalk hill in Hampshire, and the warrens, the road, and the river crossing correspond to places a walker can still find. Readers and scholars have mapped the rabbits' route against the Ordnance Survey and it holds. The geography was never a fiction; only the tenants were.
watership-down-1978.prism: A story checkable against a map carries a bill the map eventually presents. The downs the book preserved in 1972 have been under development pressure ever since, and fidelity to a real place means you can measure exactly what has gone.

nosferatu-the-vampyre-1979.gazette: Herzog's plague sequence required some 11,000 rats, imported and dyed grey before they reached the square at Delft. The Dutch city had refused the shoot on those grounds, and the production went ahead nearby. The rats are the single most documented fact of the film's making.

the-post-2017.gazette: The Pentagon Papers reached the Washington Post in June 1971, days after an injunction had already stopped the New York Times from publishing. Katharine Graham was then the paper's publisher and Ben Bradlee its executive editor, deciding whether to run classified material while the company's stock offering was in progress. The Supreme Court ruled for the newspapers within two weeks.

happy-as-lazzaro-2018.gazette: Italy abolished sharecropping by law in 1982, but on at least one tobacco estate the workers were never told. The case surfaced when investigators found a marchesa's tenants still settling accounts under a system that had ended years earlier. Rohrwacher took the report and built a film on it.
happy-as-lazzaro-2018.prism: The scheme required no fences and no guards, only the withholding of a single piece of public information. Freedom you have not been informed of is, in practice, a document filed somewhere you will never look.

the-spy-gone-north-2018.gazette: Park Chae-seo, code-named Black Venus, operated in North Korea through the mid-1990s posing as a businessman and reached the upper reaches of the regime. His work overlapped with the 1997 'North Wind' affair, in which South Korean operatives were found to have sought a border provocation ahead of the presidential election. Park was arrested and imprisoned by his own side.

dark-waters-2019.gazette: Robert Bilott, a corporate defense attorney in Cincinnati, filed against DuPont over C8 contamination in the Ohio River valley and spent the better part of two decades on the case. Discovery produced internal company documents on the chemical's effects going back years, and a court-ordered health study followed tens of thousands of residents. The compound is now detectable in the blood of most people on earth.

hustlers-2019.gazette: Jessica Pressler's 2015 magazine piece laid out how a group of New York dancers drugged Wall Street clients and ran up their credit cards, drawing on interviews and the resulting prosecutions. The scheme took shape after 2008, when the finance money that had sustained the clubs thinned out. Charges, pleas, and sentences followed in the New York courts.
hustlers-2019.prism: The women on trial were the only participants in that ecosystem whose extraction of money from finance guys was illegal. That asymmetry is the story's actual subject, and the reporting is what makes it impossible to argue with.
